$comment: Maintainer notes — stripped from the merged settings.json by install.sh; never shipped to a user's config.

These auto-approve selected rtk display forms so common reads do not add prompt friction. No broad find or git branch approval: find accepts -exec/-delete and branch accepts deletion/rename. Mutating/outbound forms (rtk curl/aws/psql/docker, rtk git push, rtk git fetch) are deliberately NOT here and still prompt.

On the two search verbs — the criterion is whether the UNDERLYING tool has an exec primitive, since these are prefix rules that approve every suffix. `rtk grep` always dispatches to the system grep (verified on 0.49.0: rg-only --glob and GNU-only -P both bounce off BSD grep, and --pre is rejected rather than run), and grep can neither exec nor write, so `Bash(rtk grep:*)` is the same risk class as the `Bash(rtk read:*)` already here.

`Bash(rtk rg:*)` is DIFFERENT and is only safe because command-guard backs it. ripgrep can be made to run an arbitrary binary three ways, all confirmed live: `--pre <cmd>`, `--hostname-bin <cmd>`, and RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH (which points rg at a file of flags, injecting --pre with neither flag visible in the command text). command-guard's detectSearchExec blocks all three at PreToolUse (exit 2). It is carried anyway because rg is the highest-value rewrite after `rtk read` — ~19x grep's saving per call in the `rtk gain` sample — so skipping it would forfeit most of the search savings. HARD DEPENDENCY: this allow rule and that block ship together. Never approve rtk rg in a profile without command-guard, and re-verify both the grep dispatch and the rg exec-flag block before bumping the rtk floor.

Note for users: rtk truncates long search output and stashes the remainder in its platform data directory (verified on macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/rtk/recall.db, mode 0600), retrievable later via `rtk recall <id>`. So matched lines outlive the session on disk. rtk-safe refuses to rewrite a grep/rg whose literal text names a credential path (see CRED_PATH in rtk-safe.ts), which keeps the obvious case out of that store.

On `rtk read`: kept here even though it can read arbitrary files. The secure-settings Read(...) deny only binds to readers Claude Code recognizes (cat/head/tail/sed), so unrecognized readers (xxd/base64/od/python -c, and rtk read) bypass it regardless — gating rtk read would cost the highest-volume read path (~31% of rtk's token savings per `rtk gain`) for ~zero security gain. The credential case that actually occurs (the model typing `cat <credpath>`) is handled upstream by rtk-safe.ts, which refuses to rewrite cat/head of credential paths so they stay as `cat` and stay denied.
